Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

glazelite 0.1.2

First release prepared for CRAN.

Closer to jsonlite

  • toJSON() writes Date objects and date-times (POSIXct, POSIXlt), with the Date, POSIXt and UTC arguments of jsonlite.
  • New unbox() marks single values that should be written as scalars.
  • digits rounds numbers as jsonlite does: a number gives decimal digits and I(n) significant digits. The default, NA, still keeps full precision.
  • NULL is written as {} by default (null = "null" writes null), list elements without a name are keyed by their position, and character row names of data frames are written as _row (see rownames).
  • pretty also accepts the number of spaces to indent by.
  • fromJSON(), read_json() and stream_in() gain simplifyMatrix: regular arrays of arrays become matrices and higher-dimensional arrays, so fromJSON(toJSON(x)) returns a matrix or array x unchanged.
  • read_json() returns nested lists unless simplifyVector = TRUE, as in jsonlite. simplifyDataFrame and simplifyMatrix default to simplifyVector.
  • New prettify(), minify() and validate().
  • stream_out() and stream_in() take con, a file path or a connection, and accept verbose. stream_out() can write to connections such as gzfile(). The argument was called path before.
  • write_json() and stream_out() pass their options on to toJSON() through ....
  • toJSON() returns an object of class c("glazelite_json", "json") that prints as plain JSON text.

Reading

  • fromJSON(), read_json() and stream_in() simplify arrays to vectors, matrices and data frames in C++ while converting the parsed document, which makes reading several times faster than before.
  • Simplification follows the JSON structure: an array of arrays of records is a list of data frames, integer arrays containing null stay integer, and [{}, {}] is a data frame with two rows and no columns.
  • Truncated documents, input with content after the document, and empty input are rejected instead of returning a partial result.
  • stream_in() without a handler reads all lines and parses them together; pagesize applies to pages passed to a handler. A connection that is not yet open is opened once, instead of re-reading its first page indefinitely.

Writing

  • Data frames with matrix columns or data-frame columns are written one row at a time as nested arrays or records instead of using only their first column, and data frames whose columns differ in length are rejected.
  • An empty named list is written as {}.
  • File paths are tilde-expanded.
  • Interrupting a long write no longer leaves the output file open; errors and interrupts are raised only after the native writer has released its resources.

Package

  • All exported functions document their return value and have runnable examples.
  • Bundle only the Glaze headers needed for JSON, and credit the authors of the third-party code contained in Glaze (see inst/COPYRIGHTS).
  • The package has a logo and a website at https://ninohardt.github.io/glazelite/.

glazelite 0.1.1

  • Write one-dimensional and higher-dimensional atomic arrays in their existing dimension order, preserving singleton and empty dimensions without copying.
  • Preserve length-one values wrapped in I() when auto_unbox = TRUE.
  • Add factor = "integer" and always_decimal to the JSON and NDJSON writers.
  • Add buffered pretty output to toJSON() and write_json().
  • Accept digits = NA for full round-trip precision and reject unsupported rounding requests explicitly.
  • Add regression checks for Stan-compatible shapes, types, and file streaming.
